# A chat for analytics users

`AnalyticsChat` is a chat for people who work with data. The conversation is always there; everything else appears only when you pass its prop:

- `sessions`: saved conversations, listed in a Conversations panel to search, filter, sort and group, and each conversation saved as it goes.
- `attachFiles`: a `+` button, and files dropped or pasted on the box. Any file is offered (`accept` narrows the picker); your function says which became data (a `DataRef`), which is a picture to show as a thumbnail (`attachment`), which it handled itself (`taken`) and why the others did not.
- `browse`: an "Add data" button and a Data panel with tables (`ObjectBrowser`) and files (`FileBrowser`). Names go to the agent, never values.
- `agents`: a Model menu, and one Agent setup menu whose sections (Agent, Skills, Connectors) open in place, filled from `DescribeAgents`. Short lists are menus in the composer; each ends in "View all…" or "Manage…", which opens its panel on the rail to the right.
- `speech`: a microphone that dictates, and a Talk button for a spoken conversation that sends after a pause, reads the reply and listens again. It stops when a reply needs a decision.

Send is a round arrow. With none of these props it is a plain conversation with no workspace.

The agent says what a person may choose. `offer` on `toolCallingAgent` lists the models, skills (text added to the system prompt while on) and connectors (sets of tools, on or off). The backend refuses anything it did not list:

`agent.ts`:

```ts
import { type AgentBackend, type DescribesAgents, type ModelChunk, type ToolCallingAgentOptions, dataTools, toolCallingAgent } from "@surfaces-ui/agent";
import type { DataSource } from "@surfaces-ui/data";

/**
 * What a person may choose for this agent: two models, two skills and one
 * connector. The backend checks every turn against it; the client is never
 * trusted to turn on something not listed.
 */
export function analystAgent(dataSource: DataSource, complete: ToolCallingAgentOptions["complete"]): AgentBackend & DescribesAgents {
  const tools = dataTools(dataSource);
  return toolCallingAgent({
    system: "You answer questions about the person's data.",
    tools,
    complete,
    offer: {
      id: "analyst",
      name: "Analyst",
      models: [
        { id: "claude-sonnet-5-5", label: "Claude Sonnet 5.5" },
        { id: "claude-opus-5-5", label: "Claude Opus 5.5" },
      ],
      defaultModel: "claude-sonnet-5-5",
      skills: [
        { id: "charts", name: "Chart standards", text: "Bars start at zero. One y scale.", defaultOn: true },
        { id: "terse", name: "Short answers", text: "Answer in two sentences at most.", defaultOn: false },
      ],
      // Tools no connector names are always on; these are on only while the connector is.
      connectors: [{ id: "catalog", name: "Data catalog", description: "List and describe tables", tools: tools.map((t) => t.name) }],
    },
  });
}

/** A stand-in for a model, for the test: it says which model it was asked to be. */
export async function* echoModel({ model }: { model?: string }): AsyncIterable<ModelChunk> {
  yield { type: "text", delta: `Answered by ${model}.` };
  yield { type: "done", model: model ?? "" };
}
```

The page asks the agent what it offers and keeps conversations in a surface library, so they also show in a Library as saved surfaces of kind conversation. With your server, `connectAgent({ baseUrl })` from `@surfaces-ui/client-connect` has both `send` and `describeAgents`:

`App.tsx`:

```tsx
import { AnalyticsChat, type AttachResult, browserSpeech, librarySessions } from "@surfaces-ui/chat";
import type { AgentBackend, DescribesAgents } from "@surfaces-ui/agent";
import { DataSourceProvider } from "@surfaces-ui/components";
import { type DataSource, type SurfaceLibrary } from "@surfaces-ui/data";
import type { AgentInfo } from "@surfaces-ui/proto";
import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";

export interface AnalyticsChatPageProps {
  /** `connectAgent({ baseUrl })` in a real app; anything with `send` and `describeAgents`. */
  agent: AgentBackend & DescribesAgents;
  dataSource: DataSource;
  /** Where conversations are kept: `memorySurfaceLibrary({ storage: browserStorage() })`, or your server's library. */
  library: SurfaceLibrary;
  sourceId: string;
  /** Turn on voice only when the person chose it: the browser's speech service may send audio away. */
  voice?: boolean;
}

export function AnalyticsChatPage({ agent, dataSource, library, sourceId, voice }: AnalyticsChatPageProps) {
  const [agents, setAgents] = useState<AgentInfo[]>([]);
  useEffect(() => {
    void agent.describeAgents().then((r) => setAgents(r.agents));
  }, [agent]);
  const sessions = useMemo(() => librarySessions(library), [library]);
  const speech = useMemo(() => (voice ? browserSpeech() : undefined), [voice]);

  // Your own rule for files: here every file is named and refused, since this server reads only its own tables.
  const attachFiles = async (files: File[]): Promise<AttachResult[]> => files.map((file) => ({ file, error: "This server reads only its own tables." }));

  return (
    <DataSourceProvider dataSource={dataSource}>
      <AnalyticsChat
        agent={agent}
        agents={agents}
        sessions={sessions}
        attachFiles={attachFiles}
        browse={{ sourceId }}
        speech={speech}
        starters={["What tables are there?"]}
        height={640}
      />
    </DataSourceProvider>
  );
}
```

Voice listens only once the person agrees: pass `speechConsent` and the microphone's first press asks, saying where audio goes; or pass `speech` only after they turned it on. `browserSpeech()` uses the browser's own speech service; in Chrome that sends audio to Google, and its `label` says so. Pass your own `SpeechAdapter` to use another service.

The test picks a model from the menu, sends a question, sees that the turn ran on that model, and finds the conversation in the library:

`analytics-chat.test.tsx`:

```tsx
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { memoryDataSource, memorySurfaceLibrary } from "@surfaces-ui/data";
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { AnalyticsChatPage } from "./App.js";
import { analystAgent, echoModel } from "./agent.js";

afterEach(cleanup);

describe("analytics chat recipe", () => {
  it("offers the agent's models and skills, runs a turn on the chosen model, and keeps the conversation", async () => {
    const dataSource = memoryDataSource({ sourceId: "shop", tables: { orders: [{ order_id: 1, amount: 10 }] } });
    const library = memorySurfaceLibrary();
    render(<AnalyticsChatPage agent={analystAgent(dataSource, echoModel)} dataSource={dataSource} library={library} sourceId="shop" />);

    fireEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Model: Claude Sonnet 5.5" }));
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: /Claude Opus 5.5/ }));
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "How many orders?" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send" }));
    expect(await screen.findByText("Answered by claude-opus-5-5.")).toBeTruthy();

    // Saved to the library as a conversation, titled from the question.
    await waitFor(async () => expect((await library.listSurfaces({})).surfaces.map((s) => s.title)).toEqual(["How many orders?"]));
  });
});
```

Not verified here: speech in a real browser (the chat package tests the loop with a fake adapter), and a live model.
